explanation: Parallel lines have the same slope, so line ℓ has slope 8. Since it passes through (0, 0), its equation is y = 8x. At x = 3, d = 8(3) = 24.
Each week Brian saves (2/5)(215) = 86 dollars. Over 9 weeks he saves 9 · 86 = 774 dollars. Be careful not to stop at the weekly amount.
Distribute: y = (29/3)x + 10/3 + 5x. The x-terms combine to (29/3 + 15/3)x = (44/3)x, so the slope is 44/3. The constant 10/3 is the y-intercept, not part of the slope.
Staining the fence twice means covering 2w square feet. At 170 square feet per gallon, S = 2w/170 = w/85. Choice A only covers the fence once.

fix.prompt: One gallon of stain will cover 170 square feet of a surface. A yard has a total fence area of w square feet. Which equation represents the total amount of stain S, in gallons, needed to stain the fence in this yard twice?

explanation: When x = 0 (the moment the height was first measured), f(0) = 4, so 4 is the estimated height in feet at the first measurement. The growth per year is the slope 8, not 4.
The mean of the four scores is (G + 85 + 78 + 98)/4, and it must be at least 90, so (G + 85 + 78 + 98)/4 ≥ 90. Choice B wrongly multiplies G by 4.
Infinitely many solutions means the two equations are the same line. Multiplying the first equation by 3 gives (3/2)x + y = 1/2, which has the same form as ax + y = c. So a = 3/2 (and c = 1/2).
The cost is $11 for each of d days, which is 11d, plus a single $10 fee, so c = 11d + 10. Choice A wrongly adds the fee to the number of days before multiplying.

The graph of y = f(x) + 14 has y-intercept 2 and passes through (8, 0), so its slope is -2/8 = -1/4 and f(x) + 14 = -(1/4)x + 2. Subtracting 14 gives f(x) = -(1/4)x - 12. Choice C is the equation of the graphed line itself, not f.

The total 32 is measured in cups, so each term is a number of cups. Since y is the number of large jars, 5 must be the cups per large jar, and 5y is the total cups of broth in the large jars. Choice A describes y alone.
The distance was at least 1,510 miles and at most 4,130 miles, so 1,510 ≤ d ≤ 4,130.
The boiling point starts at 212°F and drops 1°F for every 550 feet, so after x feet it has dropped x/550 degrees: B = 212 - x/550. Choice C adds instead of subtracting.
Test (-4, 0): -4(-4) + 4 = 20, and 0 < 20 is true. The other points fail: (0, 5) gives 5 < 4, (2, 1) gives 1 < -4, and (2, -1) gives -1 < -4, all false.

A system has no solution when the lines are parallel and distinct: same slope, different y-intercept. -7x + y = 21 becomes y = 7x + 21, with slope 7 and intercept 21 instead of 18. Choice D is the same line (infinitely many solutions), and choices A and B have slope 21.
The slope is (13 - 5)/(3 - 1) = 4. Using (1, 5): 5 = 4 + b, so b = 1 and f(x) = 4x + 1. Check: f(5) = 21.
Set 14 + 4x = 58. Then 4x = 44, so x = 11 games.
On the graph, the point with 4 pounds of tangerines (x = 4) has y = 10, so he bought 10 pounds of lemons. Check with the line y = 18 - 2x: 18 - 8 = 10.
Substitute t = 2: d = 30(2) = 60 feet. Choice B adds 2 instead of multiplying.
Substitute y = 4x + 1 into the second equation: 4(4x + 1) = 15x - 8, so 16x + 4 = 15x - 8 and x = -12. Then y = 4(-12) + 1 = -47, and x - y = -12 - (-47) = 35.
Reading the graph at x = 60 gives y = 175. The line starts at 100 and rises 25 for every 20 rings, so the cost is 100 + (5/4)(60) = 175 dollars.
"8 times a number x" is 8x, and "3 more than" that is 8x + 3, which equals 83. Choice C swaps the roles of 3 and 8.
Subtract the second equation from the first: (7x - 4x) + (-5y + 8y) = 4 - 9, which gives 3x + 3y = -5. No need to solve for x and y separately.
The line crosses the y-axis at (0, -8) and the x-axis at (-8, 0), so its slope is (0 - (-8))/(-8 - 0) = -1. The equation is y = -x - 8.
The total budget is the departmental part plus the other part: x = y + 201. Rearranged, x - y = 201. Choice A would make the total smaller than its parts.
Set the expressions equal: -(1/5)x = (1/7)x. The only way two different multiples of x are equal is x = 0 (then y = 0 too).
From 4x = 20, x = 5. Then -15 + y = -7, so y = 8, and x + y = 13.
The y-intercept is where the line crosses the y-axis. On the graph this happens at y = 8, so the y-intercept is (0, 8).
After 365 days the gain is between 2(365) = 730 and 3(365) = 1,095 pounds. Adding the 200-pound birth weight gives 930 < w < 1,295. Choice C forgets the birth weight.
Expand the left side: 3a - ax - b. For infinitely many solutions, the x-coefficients and constants must match: -a = -2 gives a = 2, and 3a - b = -1 gives 6 - b = -1, so b = 7.

Let the pieces have masses x and y grams: x + y = 50 and 0.30x + 0.80y = 0.50(50) = 25. Substituting x = 50 - y gives 15 + 0.5y = 25, so y = 20 grams. The silicon in that piece is 0.80(20) = 16.0 grams. Choice C is the mass of the whole second piece, not its silicon.
Volunteers = total - donors = 165 - 130 = 35.
Subtract 6 from both sides: 4x = 12. Both equations give x = 3.
The cost for n attendees is 35 + 10.25n, which must be at most 300. So 10.25n ≤ 265 and n ≤ 25.85... Since n is a whole number, the greatest possible value is 25.
50/12 ≈ 4.17, so 4 packages (48 rolls) are not enough. The minimum is 5 packages (60 rolls).

Solving for y gives y = -(a/b)x + 1, so the y-intercept is 1. Because 0 < a < b, the slope -a/b is between -1 and 0: the line falls, but less steeply than slope -1. Only graph C crosses the y-axis at 1 with a gentle downward slope.

explanation: Substitute the endpoints of 0.5 ≤ p ≤ 0.85: H = 120(0.5) + 60 = 120 and H = 120(0.85) + 60 = 162. So 120 ≤ H ≤ 162. Choice C uses p = 0 (resting rate) as the lower bound.

The left side is 2kx - 2n. A linear equation has no solution when the x-coefficients match but the constants differ. So 2k = -28/15, giving k = -14/15. The constants differ because -2n = -36/19 would need n = 18/19, which is not greater than 1.
Substitute: x = 0 gives y = 40, x = 1 gives y = 36, and x = 2 gives y = 32, which matches table C. Table B increases by 4 each time, but the slope -4 means y must decrease.
Over 12 days the plant grew 12 · 1.20 = 14.4 cm. Its starting height was 36.8 - 14.4 = 22.4 cm.
f(0) = 29 gives the y-intercept 29, and f(x) increases by 3 each time x increases by 1, so the slope is 3: f(x) = 3x + 29.

The point with 0 wallflowers is at 16 cornflowers, meaning 16 cornflowers cost exactly $24.00. So one cornflower costs 24/16 = 1.50 dollars. (Similarly, 12 wallflowers cost $24, so each wallflower is $2.00.)

To maximize large candles, buy exactly 200 candles total, with L large and 200 - L small. Then 4.90(200 - L) + 11.60L ≤ 2,200, so 980 + 6.70L ≤ 2,200 and L ≤ 182.09... The greatest whole number is 182.
Treat (x + 6) as one quantity: (1/3 - 1/2)(x + 6) = -(1/6)(x + 6) = -8. So x + 6 = 48 and x = 42.
"At most 17 less than 5 times y" means x ≤ 5y - 17. With y = 3, x ≤ 15 - 17 = -2, so the greatest possible value of x is -2.
x forks at $0.04 each cost 0.04x, and y plates at $0.48 each cost 0.48y. Their total is 661.76, so 0.04x + 0.48y = 661.76. Choice C swaps the prices.

From x = -2s to x = -s, y drops by 3, so the slope is -3/s. At x = s, y = 15 = -3 + b, so b = 18 and y = -(3/s)x + 18. Multiplying by s gives sy = -3x + 18s, or 3x + sy = 18s. Check (-2s, 24): -6s + 24s = 18s.
Let c be correct and i incorrect answers: c + i = 40 and 2c - i = 50. Adding the equations gives 3c = 90, so c = 30 (and i = 10, check: 60 - 10 = 50).
Before the coupon, the total was 27 + 63 = 90 dollars. Each of the 9 bins cost 90/9 = 10 dollars.

The line hits the x-axis at (60, 0) and the y-axis at (0, 40). For 8x + 12y = 480: x = 60 gives 480 and y = 40 gives 480, so both intercepts match. Choice D gives intercepts (40, 0) and (0, 60), which is reversed.
4x is the cost of the binders and 3y is the cost of the notebooks, so their sum, 24, is the total cost in dollars of all binders and notebooks.

Rewrite the first equation as 48x - 102y = 24 and the second as 16x + ry = 1/6. Multiply the second by 3: 48x + 3ry = 1/2. No solution requires matching coefficients with different constants, so 3r = -102 and r = -34 (and 24 ≠ 1/2, so the lines are distinct).
Solving gives 2x = 6, so x = 3. A linear equation with a nonzero x-coefficient has exactly one solution.
Each mile takes 5.7 minutes, so x miles take 5.7x minutes: m(x) = 5.7x. Adding 5.7 (choice B) would mean each extra mile takes only 1 minute.
f increases by 64 for each 1 increase in x, so a = 64. From f(2) = 0: 128 + b = 0, so b = -128. Then a - b = 64 - (-128) = 192.
Subtract 40 from both sides: x = 95 - 40 = 55.
From the first equation, y = 9x + 13. Substitute into 5x = 2y: 5x = 18x + 26, so x = -2 and y = 9(-2) + 13 = -5. Check: 5(-2) = 2(-5). Choice D swaps x and y.
Substitute y = 19: 19 = 4x - 9, so 4x = 28 and x = 7. The solution is (7, 19).

The rate of change is (1.9 - 4)/(13 - 0) = -2.1/13 = -21/130 million barrels per year, and f(0) = 4. So f(t) = -(21/130)t + 4. Choices A and B have positive slopes, which would mean production increased.
Every x in table A (19, 20, 21) is less than 22, and each y is 1 less than its x, so y < x holds. Table B has y > x, and tables C and D have x values above 22.
The two equal parts together are 115 - 47 = 68 cm, so each is 68/2 = 34 cm.
Subtract the second equation from the first: 18x = -24, so x = -4/3. Then y = 72 - 6(-4/3) = 72 + 8 = 80. Check: 24(-4/3) + 80 = -32 + 80 = 48.
From 2x = 12, x = 6, so 9x = 54.
The slope through the points is (-5 - 3)/(4 - (-2)) = -8/6 = -4/3. Check C: f(-2) = 8/3 + 1/3 = 3 and f(4) = -16/3 + 1/3 = -5. Choice D passes through (4, -5) but gives f(-2) = 4.
The boundary values 7x - 4 are 17, 31, and 52 for x = 3, 5, and 8. Table D has y = 21, 35, 56, all greater. Table B equals the boundary (not greater), and tables A and C each have a value too small.

Let a be adult and c child tickets: a + c = 30 and 12a + 8c = 300. Substituting c = 30 - a gives 4a + 240 = 300, so a = 15. Adult tickets brought in 15 · 12 = 180 dollars. Don't stop at 15, which is the number of tickets.
The line starts at the origin and passes through (1, 2) and (3, 6), so d increases by 2 feet each minute with no starting distance: d = 2m. Choice D would start at 2 feet.
Combine like terms: -2(t + 3) = 38, so t + 3 = -19 and t = -22.

Line g passes through (-10, 12) and (0, 1), so its slope is -11/10 and y = -(11/10)x + 1, or 11x + 10y = 10. For infinitely many solutions, line k must be the same line; multiplying by 15 gives 165x + 150y = 150. So p = 150, w = 150, and p + w = 300.

The total 36 is in cups of jam, so each term counts cups. With y large containers, 6 is the cups per large container, so 6y is the total cups of jam in the large containers. Choice A describes y alone.
Expand: 12x - 36 = -3x - 36. Then 15x = 0, so x = 0 is the only solution. The x-coefficients differ, so there is exactly one solution.
Let s be students and c chaperones: s + c = 83 and 8.5s + 12c = 730. Substituting c = 83 - s gives 996 - 3.5s = 730, so s = 76. Check: 8.5(76) + 12(7) = 646 + 84 = 730.
